prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant: River Intake Pump Station (Ironwood)/Raw Water Screen Channel–High Service Pump Header; distribution excluded. Intake requires demand/depth/equipment/downstream permissives; faults/local control inhibit; lost permissives alarm/stop. Screen sends Rake Torque Snapshot; high-high requires field confirmation. Chief Operator authorizes Storm Intake Mode/urgent-dose correction/recovery; storm requires discretionary-work re-review/stability sampling. Duty Engineer approves temporary adjustments/configuration/forecasts. Maintenance preserves demand/backwash capacity; overrides require justification/monitoring/restoration.
Coagulant Dosing Skid (Marigold) sends Alum Batch Ticket; Laboratory Technician verifies lots. Dose incrementally with verified feedback; loss requires last-safe/approved-fixed dosing/grabs. North Filter Gallery (Cobalt)/South Filter Gallery receive advisories; South sends Filter Run Exception Note. Backwash considers duration/headloss/turbidity/upstream; return requires compliant rinse/stability. Backwash Recovery Tank returns require consequential-event sampling.
Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (Sparrow) accepts custody-controlled six-location/maintenance samples; sends checked Jar Test Photograph Set. Laboratory Technician sends Sample Chain Slip, reports acceptance/sampling concerns, confirms residuals; discrepancies documented, compromised results troubleshooting-only; failed checks require correction/rejection; field readings provisional, contradictions notify Chief Operator.
Maintenance Planner (Quarry) verifies orders/isolations/parts/closure; approved window/responsibility/return-condition required. Craft verifies all-energy lockout locally; operations acknowledges. Handover documents restrictions. Return evidence: inspections/tests/instruments/samples/operator acceptance; temporary items removed/formally accepted. Failed tests keep orders open; Chief Operator decides isolation/restriction.
SCADA Historian Server (Lantern) retains timestamped/pre-post performance; Chief Operator confirms chlorine-control/residual/level consistency before normal disinfection. Chlorine Contact Basin maintains required contact time versus production/level/residual; chlorine changes gradual. Chlorine Residual Alarm pauses maintenance pending operations diagnosis; verify analyzer flow/grab comparison; hold production increases. Clearwell Level Controller protects contact/reserve/suction; low-level interlocks prevent unsafe depletion; high alarms permit overflow prevention.
Chemical Supplier Driver sends Chlorine Cylinder Seal Log before unloading; controlled routes/operator-observed access, transfer inspections, chlorine ventilation/gas-monitoring/communications required. Residuals Hauler removes material. Distribution Dispatcher receives restrictions/maintenance notice.

New part:
S134: The Clearwell Level Controller sends the Clearwell Diver Entry Permit when level and isolation prerequisites have been verified by the control system.
S135: Clearwell level changes are trended against filter production and high-service demand so that slow instrumentation errors can be distinguished from actual storage changes.
S136: The High Service Pump Header is identified in voice radio traffic by the alias Juniper when operators need a short confirmation name.
S137: The High Service Pump Header sequences available pumps to meet distribution demand while avoiding unnecessary starts, short cycling, and operation near unstable portions of the pump curves.
S138: Lead and lag pump assignments are rotated according to runtime, availability, and any operating restriction entered by the Chief Operator.
S139: Header pressure control uses a paced response so that pump starts, pump speed changes, and valve movements do not create avoidable pressure transients in the distribution system.
S140: The High Service Pump Header produces the Pump Bearing Vibration Clip after a configured vibration threshold is exceeded during pump operation.
S141: If a high-service pump trips, the remaining available pumps are evaluated automatically against the current pressure setpoint before another unit is started.
S142: The North Distribution Pressure Station and South Distribution Pressure Station receive pressure support through coordinated setpoints that reflect system demand and storage conditions.
S143: The Distribution Dispatcher is identified by the alias Falcon during pressure coordination calls with plant staff.
S144: The Distribution Dispatcher communicates expected demand changes, main break impacts, and pressure complaints so that plant pumping decisions match field conditions.
S145: During Storm Intake Mode, operators watch the relationship between raw water quality, filter loading, disinfectant demand, and high-service pumping to avoid forcing production beyond treatment capability.
S146: Abnormal clearwell level, loss of residual, loss of pump header pressure, or conflicting instrument readings require the Duty Engineer to review the operating condition before setpoints are changed outside normal ranges.
S147: The SCADA Historian Server stores residual, level, pressure, and pump status data at sufficient resolution to support event reconstruction after alarms or customer pressure complaints.
S148: Manual operation is allowed only when the operator can maintain residual targets, clearwell limits, and distribution pressure with direct observation of the affected indications.
S149: Return to automatic control requires stable chlorine residual, stable clearwell level response, and confirmed high-service pressure control for a period set by the Chief Operator.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
